PullRequest.Title: eslint: fix bracket notation in language extensions
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- replace identifier-safe bracket notation with dot notation across the 22 files in the **Language feature extensions** exclusion group
- remove the completed group from `.eslint-allowed-bracket-notation-files`

This is a mechanical cleanup for `local/code-no-bracket-notation-for-identifiers` with no intended behavior changes.

## Validation

- targeted ESLint across all 22 affected files
- targeted hygiene checks
- compiled all 10 affected extension build targets
- `npm run transpile-client`
- extension-host suites:
  - Emmet: 176 passing
  - Markdown: 95 passing, 1 pending
  - TypeScript: 53 passing, 8 pending
  - CSS and HTML runners completed successfully with 0 tests discovered

## Stacking

Stacked on #334756 and intended to merge after that PR.

Scenarios.Scenario: Activating the CSS, HTML, JSON, and Markdown language-feature extensions and starting their language servers
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Extension activation sets the localization environment variable, constructs each language client, and awaits server startup before the extension is ready. The changed property accesses do not add any step to that path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start the CSS, HTML, JSON, or Markdown language server using the existing language-client transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing server process/worker per activated extension, not per document.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same server was started with the same environment value and IPC transport; bracket notation read/wrote the identical property.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Server startup is awaited on activation and is therefore on each extension's cold-start path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Language-client initialization and subsequent communication with each language server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One initialization exchange per server plus existing feature requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical client/server initialization and request flow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Initialization must complete before language features are ready.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read JSON extension package metadata and initialize the JSON schema-cache directory.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One package read and at most one recursive directory creation per JSON extension activation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical filesystem work; only environment/header property syntax changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both complete before the JSON client starts.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The number of language-feature extensions activated in a session; each affected extension performs its own existing one-time startup, independent of document count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each extension starts at most its existing single language-server process/worker when activated; extensions may activate independently, with no limiter or concurrency change in this diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold activation performs the existing module/process startup. Warm sessions retain the existing client/server lifecycle. JSON also creates/opens its existing schema-cache directory; no cache key, invalidation, hit behavior, or negative caching changes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: every affected startup hunk replaces bracket notation with dot notation for the same valid identifier, and surrounding startup code is unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual activation timing varies by host and whether each language is used, but the diff adds no operation, allocation, or boundary call.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: startup cardinality, critical-path work, IPC, subprocesses, and filesystem behavior are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Typing in HTML/CSS/JS/TS documents with HTML auto-insertion and Emmet completion or expansion enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: HTML character changes may schedule a 100 ms delayed auto-insert LSP request; Emmet completion/expansion reads configuration and may parse the document before producing edits. The changed accesses remain inline property reads and do not add work or move parsing/IPC onto a hotter path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the existing HTML AutoInsertRequest to the language server after a qualifying '=', '>', or '/' edit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one request after the existing 100 ms replacement timeout for the latest qualifying edit.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same boolean configuration flags selected the same request path with identical timeout coalescing.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The asynchronous response gates insertion but does not block raw typing.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Dispatch vscode.executeDocumentSymbolProvider for applicable JS/TS Emmet completion candidates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one existing command dispatch per applicable completion invocation; not used for all languages or obvious-noise abbreviations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same configuration values and conditions reached this command; property notation alone does not change dispatch frequency.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Its promise gates the Emmet completion result on that path.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Typing events, document size for existing parsing, completion item count, and cursor/selection count for expansion. Effective event cardinality is unchanged.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: HTML auto-insert keeps one replaceable timeout and issues at most one request for the latest qualifying edit after the delay. Emmet completion returns one promise per completion invocation and preserves its existing symbol-provider request conditions.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Emmet retains the existing root-node/partial-stylesheet parsing choices and completion state; HTML keeps the existing coalescing timeout. No cache or coalescing key changed.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: hot-path reads target identical keys, while debounce, parsing selection, loop counts, and async command placement are unchanged.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Document sizes and completion frequency vary, but the unchanged branches and partial-parse threshold make the absence of a new mechanism clear.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: no extra per-keystroke work, parsing, request fan-out, or synchronous UI work is introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Resolving remote JSON schemas with the on-disk ETag cache
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A requested schema performs the existing HTTP request; successful ETag responses may be written to disk, and 304 responses read cached content before returning to the language server.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch a JSON schema with xhr, including a conditional ETag header when available.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing HTTP flow per requested schema URI invocation, with up to the existing redirect limit of five.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same response header named 'etag' was read through bracket notation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Schema content cannot be returned until the request or fallback completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write successful ETag schema responses and read cached content after HTTP 304.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one existing write for an ETag-bearing response or one existing read on a 304 for each request flow.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical cache hit/miss and I/O behavior because response.headers['etag'] and response.headers.etag select the same key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cache I/O is awaited before returning the relevant schema result.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Distinct schema URIs requested by open JSON documents; effective cardinality remains one existing request flow per schema request, subject to the existing ETag cache.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No limiter, batching, or coalescing logic is changed; request concurrency remains whatever the existing schema requester invokes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold requests fetch content and write it when an ETag exists. Warm requests send the ETag and read cached content on 304. The cache key remains URI plus ETag, and clear/retry behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the only changed line on this path reads the same ETag field and leaves all network/cache control flow intact.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Schema counts and remote latency vary by workspace, but neither request count nor cache behavior changes.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: no new network or filesystem boundary, fan-out, cache miss, or serialization cost.

Scenarios.Scenario: Rendering Markdown previews and resolving copied-file destination snippets
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Markdown preview tokenizes and renders the document, using the existing token and engine caches; copied-file destination resolution performs one regex replacement for each resolved destination before downstream copy handling.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse Markdown text into tokens and render tokens into preview HTML.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One parse on a token-cache miss and one render per preview render; warm token-cache hits avoid reparsing as before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same renderer functions were installed under the same html_block and fenced keys; dot notation changes neither token traversal nor output allocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Rendering must complete before preview HTML is available.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Markdown text/token count for rendering and the number/length of destination templates for copied files.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Engine initialization remains represented by one cached promise, tokenization remains synchronous within each render, and destination resolution remains one local operation per file; no concurrency policy changes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The MarkdownIt engine promise and single-document token cache retain the same warm-hit behavior and invalidation on contribution changes. Destination resolution has no cache before or after the diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: renderer-key and named-capture access are semantically identical and no filesystem call exists in the changed destination resolver itself.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Markdown document and copied-file counts vary, but the diff preserves all loops, regexes, cache keys, and parser invocations.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: rendering work, allocations, cache lifecycle, and per-file resolution cardinality are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Starting and communicating with tsserver, posting TypeScript telemetry, and registering merge-conflict decorations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: TypeScript startup validates the tsserver path, constructs the child environment, spawns/forks tsserver, and then uses IPC/stdio. Telemetry augments and posts existing events. Merge decoration registration creates existing decoration types on activation/configuration changes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronously verify the configured tsserver path before launch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing existsSync call per tsserver process start.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical path check; changed environment property notation occurs afterward.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: It precedes and gates process launch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Spawn or fork tsserver with the patched environment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing child process per requested tsserver process kind/start.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE, NODE_PATH, and PATH keys and values were supplied.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Language service availability depends on process launch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Exchange tsserver protocol messages and create editor decoration types through existing VS Code APIs.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing per-request tsserver messages and one splitter decoration registration per registration pass.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same process transport and same 'splitter' decoration entry were used.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Protocol responses gate TypeScript features; decoration registration occurs before conflict decoration application.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Post existing TypeScript telemetry events through the telemetry reporter.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing post per telemetry event with the same property count and values.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same version and typings properties were added before posting; only key-access syntax changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Event posting is not moved onto a new path by this diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Configured tsserver process kinds, tsserver message/event count, and merge-decoration configuration changes; no changed expression increases any cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each existing tsserver process has its existing IPC or stdio stream; telemetry remains one post per event; decoration registration remains serialized per activation/configuration callback.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is added or removed. Existing tsserver process lifetime and decoration disposal/re-registration lifecycle are unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all environment, telemetry, and decoration accesses target identical valid identifier keys, with unchanged spawn, post, disposal, and registration statements.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of server kinds, protocol requests, and telemetry events depends on workspace activity, but the before/after operation counts are exact.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: subprocess, IPC, telemetry serialization/network, and decoration lifecycle costs are unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 23 changed files and every diff page. The PR exclusively replaces bracket notation with dot notation for identifier-safe keys and removes the corresponding lint allowlist entries. Traced startup, typing/completion, schema network/cache, Markdown rendering, tsserver, telemetry, and decoration scenarios show no added work, retained state, fan-out, synchronization, cache change, or expensive-boundary movement. No findings and no qualifying regression-fix record.
